Synthetic group-start fixtures (BSD permission in LICENSE.generated).
Generated with external official Linux x64 RAR 6.24 (not bundled), tool SHA256:
71ab9088d575e438d243672fcc6d36d2f9a39f5a8d4d26e998129cea12dbf682
Official distribution: https://www.rarlab.com/rar/rarlinux-x64-624.tar.gz
Generation commands and payload algorithm: generate_group_start.py.

RAR3 and RAR5: four compressed members a.bin, b.bin, c.bin, d.bin, each
98304 bytes, grouped with -s2. Official unrar lt reports a/c independent,
b/d solid continuation. Seven 16384-byte volumes for multipart variants.
Password variants use only the synthetic test password "password". Random
crypto salt/IV means password archives are reproducible in structure/bytes
when extracted, not byte-identical archives when regenerated.
Boundary fixture is non-solid: one data file, an empty file and a directory.

Expected output is xorshift32(seed=0x86) first 49152 low bytes, repeated twice.
Per-member CRC32: 8469b249; SHA256: 04bdbf62c09c8fe4899c780f22302811a45d787bbfea06df80f7ab642876099e.
Independent official unrar p extraction returns the four concatenated expected
members for all six group fixtures, including password and multipart variants.
Tests generate their expected bytes directly rather than reusing rardecode as
an oracle. Corrupt variants mutate packed data only and remain in memory.

Additional budget fixtures keep a/b at 98304 bytes and c/d at 4096 bytes (the
first 4096 bytes of the same payload). Both group-start headers declare a 256KiB
dictionary, capped by the decoder to member size. A 4096-byte configured budget
therefore rejects a/b but permits c/d. Official unrar extraction independently
matches payload*2 + payload[:4096]*2 for both RAR versions.
